transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I… I’m having a hard time with how my face looks. Around my mouth and jaw, it looks droopy and uneven to me, especially in photos or mirrors. People say it’s fine, but I can’t really believe them. It’s gotten bad enough that I’ve been avoiding presentations and clients.
How long have you been noticing the unevenness around your mouth and jaw, and has it changed over time?

It’s been… long enough that I can’t really ignore it anymore. I keep seeing the droop around my mouth and jaw in photos and reflections. It feels more obvious to me now, even though other people say I look fine. I’ve started staying away from presentations and clients because of it.
Can you describe what exactly looks droopy or uneven around your mouth and jaw? Is it something you’ve noticed gradually over time, or did it start suddenly?

It’s mostly around the corners of my mouth and along the jaw… like one side hangs more, or doesn’t line up right. I see it in almost every photo or reflection. I don’t know if it was sudden exactly—it just became something I couldn’t stop noticing. People tell me it looks fine, but it feels really obvious to me.
Have you noticed any actual weakness or difficulty moving one side of your face, like trouble smiling or closing your eye on that side?
I… no, I don’t think so. I can move my face. It’s more that it looks wrong to me.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to check, fix, or make sure your face looks right, like adjusting your expression, taking multiple photos, or covering part of your face?

Yes… I do. Mostly before work or if there’s some family thing. I’ll check the bathroom mirror over and over, take pictures on my phone from different angles, redo my makeup or my scarf.

I ask my husband if it looks lopsided… probably more than I should. And sometimes I end up looking at photos of other women online, just comparing, seeing how bad mine looks next to theirs. It can take hours.
Have you ever had a medical evaluation to check if there is a physical or neurological reason for the asymmetry you're seeing?
Not really… I mean, no one’s done any kind of proper check for that. I’ve thought about it, but I guess I’ve mostly just kept it to myself or asked my husband.
Has the way your face looks been causing you a lot of distress, or has it affected your work, relationships, or daily life?

Yes… it has. More than I like to admit.

I cancelled a big client presentation at the last minute because I just couldn’t stand the thought of everyone looking at me. And there’ve been award-related events, networking things, that I keep missing.

It’s starting to affect my deadlines… and family gatherings too. Things are kind of falling apart around it.
Do you believe that the asymmetry around your mouth and jaw is a sign of something being seriously wrong with your health or appearance, even if others don't see it the same way?

Yes… I mean, I know people say they don’t see it, or that it’s not a big deal. But to me it looks very obvious. The droop around my mouth, my jaw looking uneven… I see it in every photo, every reflection.

I don’t know if it means something is medically wrong, exactly, but it feels like something is wrong with how I look. Enough that I can’t face presentations or clients sometimes.
Have you ever noticed any numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation in the area around your mouth or jaw, or has anyone else noticed you having trouble feeling things on that part of your face?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed numbness or tingling, at least not that I can say. No one’s mentioned anything like that to me either.

When you avoid presentations or social events, is it mainly because you feel self-conscious about how your face looks, or is it more about worrying that other people will notice and judge your appearance negatively?

It’s… both, I guess. I feel self-conscious because I can’t stop seeing the droop and the unevenness around my mouth and jaw, especially in photos or reflections.

But the part that makes me avoid things is thinking other people will notice it too… that clients will be looking at that instead of listening to me. Even when people say I look fine, it still feels obvious to me.

Would you say your main concern is about how your face looks and the possibility that others are noticing and judging it, or is it more about a feeling that something is physically wrong with your face even if others don’t see it that way?

It’s more about how it looks… I think. I can’t stop seeing the droop and the unevenness around my mouth and jaw, especially in photos or mirrors.

And then I worry other people will notice it too, or judge me for it. Even when they say I look fine, it still feels really obvious to me. That’s why I’ve been avoiding presentations and clients.

When you think about how your face looks, is your main concern that others will notice and judge your appearance, or is it more about how you see the asymmetry yourself, even if others don’t seem to notice it?

It’s… mostly how I see it myself, I think. I keep noticing the droop around my mouth and jaw in photos or reflections, and once I see it I can’t really unsee it.

But then I do worry other people will notice too, especially at work, and that’s when I start avoiding presentations or clients. Even if they say I look fine, it still feels obvious to me.
Are you also very concerned about any other parts of your body or face besides the mouth and jaw area?
No… not really. It’s mainly the mouth and jaw area. That droop, the unevenness… I see it in every photo or reflection, and it feels very obvious even when people say it isn’t.
Have you ever been extremely worried about any other parts of your body or face besides your mouth and jaw, even for a short time?
No… I don’t think so. It’s really just been this area around my mouth and jaw. The droop, the unevenness… I see it in photos and reflections, and I can’t seem to let it go.
Do you feel that your entire face looks unattractive or deformed, or is it mainly the asymmetry around your mouth and jaw that bothers you?

It’s mainly the asymmetry… around my mouth and jaw. I don’t think of my whole face as deformed, exactly. It’s that droop there — I see it in photos and reflections, and it just feels very obvious, even when people say it isn’t.
